selected.title: 12 Rue Halévy
selected.author: Tangopaso (Wikimedia Commons)
selected.shows: Full, near-frontal corner facade: rusticated bossage ground floor with round-arched openings, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor, plain ironwork balcon filant at top floor just under the mansard comble -- one of the cleanest single-image reads of the whole family's defining stack.

selected.title: Maison à loyer, 3 rue de la Paix — élévation
selected.author: César Daly (publisher); architect M. Paul Mesnard; engraver J. Penel
selected.shows: A 'Première Classe' rental building (the standard haussmannien maison à loyer type): ground-floor shopfronts, two full-width running iron balconies (2nd and 5th-floor pattern), straight mansard comble with pedimented dormers, and a flat symmetrical facade plane — the clearest single-plate demonstration of the balcon filant rule.

selected.title: Maison à loyer, 120 boulevard de Sébastopol — détails de la façade
selected.author: César Daly (publisher); architect M. Levicomte; engraver J. Penel
selected.shows: Fully measured entrance-bay detail on the flagship percée boulevard: entresol window and door surround with dimensioned mouldings, balcony-console profile with metric callouts, door hardware — usable for exact proportions of the rez-de-chaussée treatment that a photograph could not supply.

selected.title: Maison à loyer, 9 rue du Conservatoire — détail de la façade
selected.author: César Daly (publisher); architect M. Amoudru; engraver Sulpis
selected.shows: Two stacked measured window bays with cast-iron balcon-filant railings, floral rosette bandeau, and dimensioned mouldings/reveals in metres and centimetres — a second independent source for exact balcony and window proportions.

selected.title: Maison à loyer, 63 boulevard de Sébastopol — détail de la façade
selected.author: César Daly (publisher); architects MM. Garnier et Coulon; engraver Sulpis
selected.shows: Measured door/window-pediment detail with a full dimension ladder in the margin: cartouche carving, bossage coursing either side of the opening, and an arched porte-cochère lintel below — another exact-proportions source for ground-floor surrounds on the same boulevard.

selected.title: Boulevard Sebastopol
selected.author: Charles Marville
selected.shows: Genuine period photograph, corner building pavement-to-ridge in near-frontal view: straight 45-degree comble roof with segmental-pedimented dormers, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor across the whole block, ground-floor shopfronts under a classical pilastered corner surround ('Pygmalion' sign). One of the cleanest period-authentic references for the roof/balcony/cornice relationship.

selected.title: Boulevard de Sebastopol (modern)
selected.author: Thierry Bezecourt
selected.shows: Modern mild-oblique photo of a corner immeuble on boulevard de Sebastopol (pierced 1855-58): full elevation pavement-to-ridge, straight comble, two levels of continuous balcon filant, corner chamfer. Direct present-day counterpart to the Marville photographs of the same street.

selected.title: 2 boulevard Voltaire
selected.author: Lionel Allorge
selected.shows: Dead-frontal, textbook canonical elevation: straight 45-degree comble with regularly spaced pedimented dormers, continuous balcon filant at both the 2nd floor and the top floor, flat unornamented wall plane, symmetrical window bays. Ground-floor bossage is partly masked by a shop awning but the storey stack and roof are fully legible -- probably the single best reference image in this set for the cornice-to-comble relationship.

selected.title: 3 Boulevard Malesherbes, ground-floor arcade
selected.author: Tangopaso
selected.shows: Four arched ground-floor bays with regular raised bossage: each pier and voussoir band is built from cleanly coursed ashlar blocks with deep, evenly-spaced horizontal and radiating joints -- the coursing module is constant across all four bays, giving a clean real-world course-height figure. Boulevard Malesherbes was pierced 1861-1870, squarely inside the target period. Cropped to exclude the tour bus that partly blocked the original frame.

selected.title: 88 Boulevard Malesherbes, porte-cochère surround
selected.author: kenobi75
selected.shows: Third repeat of the same coursed-ashlar ground-floor socle module seen at 84 and 86 Boulevard Malesherbes -- door surround and window jambs built from regular drafted-margin blocks, clean and well lit, minimal obstruction.

selected.title: Balcon d'un immeuble parisien
selected.author: besopha (Flickr)
selected.shows: Full window opening: triangular pediment with a shell cartouche in the tympanum on console brackets, dentilled cornice, moulded architrave, and a dense cast-iron balcon filant with heart/quatrefoil scrollwork below -- a textbook console-and-fronton-over-balcon assembly.

selected.title: Rue Halevy, 12
selected.author: Tangopaso
selected.shows: Whole corner block facade near the Opera quarter: straight mansard roofline, arcaded rusticated ground floor with voussoired arches, continuous balcon filant at two levels, pilastered piano nobile, and consistent floor-to-floor treatment continuing across the party wall to the left -- good context shot for how the window-surround programme sits inside the whole elevation.

selected.title: 19 rue Auber
selected.author: Guilhem Vellut
selected.shows: Two windows with matching triangular frontons on console brackets and a palmette-frieze architrave over a shared balcon filant, plus a single restrained male-mask keystone over the arched ground-floor entry below -- shows mascarons used sparingly (one, at the door) rather than on every opening.

selected.title: Mansard roof with pedimented dormers, Paris
selected.author: Jorge Andrade
selected.shows: textbook comble a la Mansart profile: slate brisis (steep lower slope) meeting a near-flat zinc terrasson at the ridge, four evenly spaced pedimented (triangular-fronton) dormers each with a small cast-iron balustrade, souche at right, cornice with anthemion antefixes below

selected.title: Boulevard de Sebastopol
selected.author: Thierry Bezecourt
selected.shows: unbroken cornice/balcony line running at consistent height across a long row of separate buildings down Boulevard de Sebastopol — the clearest single piece of evidence in this set for the 1855 circulaire's block-alignment requirement; straight 45-degree mansard roofs throughout, no curved combles or corner domes

selected.title: Avenue de l'Opera Enfilade
selected.author: Lawrence W.K. Ho
selected.shows: long raking view down a full block showing the roof cornice, modillion band, and running balcony continuing unbroken at identical height across many distinct building facades receding into the distance — the single most legible illustration of the 1855 circulaire's mandated horizontal continuity across party walls in this set, though the exact construction date of this stretch of the avenue (built in stages 1864-1879) could not be confirmed as pre-1870

selected.title: Typical Haussmannian Facade
selected.author: Joseph Plotz
selected.shows: full elevation with a block-modillioned main cornice under a straight 45-degree slate mansard, a plain bandeau string course marking the 2nd-floor division, dense cast-iron balcon filant, and flat ashlar wall plane with minimal relief; a second, differently detailed building is visible immediately adjoining at left for comparison

selected.title: 2, boulevard Voltaire
selected.author: Lionel Allorge
selected.shows: A plain, unornamented wood double-leaf porte cochère beside a rolled-steel shop shutter and a restaurant awning -- the one 'ordinary register' entrance kept in the set, a counterweight to the grand corner buildings that otherwise dominate what Commons has catalogued for this feature.
